title: Applicability of the theory of pain-sensorimotor interactions to orofacial pain and sensorimotor behavior, and implications for orofacial pain research and management
authors: Barry J. Sessle; Greg M. Murray
journal: Journal of Oral & Facial Pain and Headache
pain_condition_detail: Orofacial pain, including temporomandibular disorders (TMD), burning mouth syndrome (BMS), persistent dentoalveolar pain, trigeminal neuropathic pain
bps_function_set: conclusion; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; justification; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: The paper uses the biopsychosocial model as the foundational framework for TOPSMI, listing biological, psychological, and sociocultural factors that influence pain-sensorimotor interactions. It describes these factors as having 'mixes and weightings' that affect CNS plasticity and sensorimotor behavior, but does not operationalize them into specific variables or measures.
integration_mechanism_summary: The paper proposes that psychosocial, genetic, epigenetic, and environmental factors influence CNS plasticity (neuroplasticity and glioplasticity), which in turn affects sensorimotor behavior and pain. The social domain is mentioned but not mechanistically integrated; the primary pathway is bio-psych with social as a contextual modifier.
conceptual_tensions_1: The paper uses 'psychosocial factors' as an umbrella term that conflates psychological (stress, anxiety) and social (economic factors, family environment) constructs without distinguishing them
conceptual_tensions_2: TOPSMI is presented as a mechanistic framework but the paper acknowledges it may be difficult to test as a whole due to the many factors involved
conceptual_tensions_3: Social domain is mentioned (sociocultural factors, socioeconomic status) but never elaborated with specific mechanisms, creating a gap between BPS rhetoric and actual coverage
additional_observations_1: The paper is primarily a biological review of orofacial pain-sensorimotor interactions, with psychological and social factors mentioned but not developed
additional_observations_2: The biopsychosocial model is used as a foundational framework for TOPSMI, but the paper does not operationalize any BPS components into specific variables or measures
additional_observations_3: The paper introduces the novel TOPSMI framework, which is an extension of the BPS model specifically for pain-sensorimotor interactions
additional_observations_4: Genetic and epigenetic factors are treated as biological factors, but the paper also notes they can be modified by psychosocial and environmental factors, suggesting a more complex interaction
synthesis_note: This paper applies the novel TOPSMI framework to orofacial pain, using the biopsychosocial model as its foundation. It provides an elaborated biological account of pain-sensorimotor interactions (nociceptive pathways, CNS plasticity, genetics, epigenetics) but treats psychological and social factors as listed influences without mechanistic depth. The social domain is particularly thin, mentioned only as 'sociocultural factors' without specific constructs or pathways. The paper acknowledges the potential unfalsifiability of TOPSMI.
coding_rationale: Typology is pseudo_bps because BPS language is used but social domain is minimal and psychological constructs are only named. Triadic integration is partial: bio-psych integration is directional via CNS plasticity, but social is loosely attached. Bio-dominant balance reflects the paper's primary focus on biological mechanisms.

bps_function_set: explanatory framework; intervention rationale; justification; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: TOPSMI operationalizes BPS by treating favorable or adverse mixes/weightings of biological, psychological, sociocultural, genetic, epigenetic and environmental factors as setting CNS plasticity and musculoskeletal function, which then shapes pain-sensorimotor behavior; clinical recommendations follow customized diagnosis/management.
integration_mechanism_summary: Psychosocial factors can set or alter CNS plasticity, descending modulation, nociceptive pathways, and musculoskeletal tissue properties; genetic and epigenetic factors modify these processes; favorable or adverse mixes set adaptive or maladaptive CNS states and sensorimotor outcomes. No single mediator is named for all three domains.
conceptual_tensions_1: TOPSMI is presented as more comprehensive and mechanistic, yet the authors state it may be difficult to formally test as a whole because many factors are involved
conceptual_tensions_2: The review extends spinal-system evidence to orofacial pain while repeatedly noting that comparable orofacial datasets are much more limited
conceptual_tensions_3: The BPS label brings in sociocultural factors, but the social evidence is thinner than the biological and psychological evidence
conceptual_tensions_4: Management is recommended as customized to individual factor mixtures, but the paper does not provide a formal measurement or coding scheme for those mixtures
conceptual_tensions_5: Prior theories are criticized for lacking a full picture, while TOPSMI is defended as mechanistic despite limited direct testing
additional_observations_1: The paper does not report formal quality assessment or risk-of-bias tools for the evidence it reviews
additional_observations_2: The main operationalization is theoretical: favorable versus adverse mix and weighting of factors sets CNS plasticity state
additional_observations_3: No named psychological instruments, pain outcome instruments, or psychosocial measurement scales are reported
additional_observations_4: The review proposes future longitudinal neuroimaging trials, biopsychosocial stratification, and gene-environment interaction models
synthesis_note: This review operationalizes BPS mainly through TOPSMI rather than through measured constructs. It gives rich biological and psychological mechanisms and a weaker sociocultural layer, so it operationalizes BPS mainly through TOPSMI rather than through measured constructs.
coding_rationale: TOPSMI is mechanistic triadic despite thin social evidence; biological content dominates, and no formal quality/risk tools or instruments are used.

title: Applicability of the theory of pain-sensorimotor interactions to orofacial pain and sensorimotor behavior, and implications for orofacial pain research and management
authors: Barry J. Sessle; Greg M. Murray
journal: Journal of Oral & Facial Pain and Headache
bps_function_set: background framing; explanatory framework; organizing principle
bps_operationalization_summary: Organizes the review into biological, psychological, and sociocultural factors sections, using BPS as theoretical foundation for TOPSMI theory. Integrates domains through mechanistic pathways involving CNS plasticity.
integration_mechanism_summary: Psychosocial, genetic, epigenetic, and environmental factors influence CNS plasticity and glioplasticity, which in turn affect musculoskeletal tissues and sensorimotor behaviors. Biological, psychological, and social factors are integrated through their effects on CNS circuits and plasticity mechanisms.
conceptual_tensions_1: Limited empirical investigation of psychosocial factors in orofacial pain models despite theoretical integration
conceptual_tensions_2: Gap between BPS theoretical framework and empirical measurement of social factors in orofacial pain research
additional_observations_1: The review emphasizes the role of CNS plasticity as the central mechanism linking biological, psychological, and social factors to sensorimotor behaviors
additional_observations_2: TOPSMI theory proposes that individual differences in biopsychosocial factor weighting determine adaptive vs maladaptive plasticity states
synthesis_note: This review operationalizes the biopsychosocial model through the Theory of Pain-Sensorimotor Interactions (TOPSMI), integrating biological, psychological, and sociocultural factors through CNS plasticity mechanisms. While biological factors are well-developed, psychological and social factors are mentioned but not extensively investigated. The review demonstrates descriptive triadic integration with mechanistic elements through neuroplasticity pathways.
coding_rationale: TOPSMI provides true integrative framework with descriptive triadic integration. Biological domain elaborated, psychological/social mentioned. Psychosocial factors mediate CNS plasticity which drives sensorimotor behaviors.
